name: Kentucky

agency.name: Kentucky Education and Labor Cabinet - Office of Workplace Standards (Wage and Hour)

rates2026.note: KRS 337.275; the state rate automatically rises to match any federal increase.

tipped.note: Employees receiving more than $30/month in tips: employer may pay the federal tipped cash wage ($2.13) if wage plus tips reach $7.25; tips belong to the employee (tip pooling among employees allowed).

source.quote: not less than seven dollars and twenty-five cents ($7.25) an hour beginning July 1, 2009.

overtime.seventhDay: Time and a half for hours worked on the 7th day when an employee is permitted to work all 7 days of a workweek and more than 40 hours that week (KRS 337.050).
overtime.exemptSalaryNote: No state salary threshold above the federal $684/week.
overtime.note: KRS 337.285 excludes retail store and restaurant/hotel/motel employees from STATE overtime; such workers remain covered by FLSA overtime if their employer is covered.

source.quote: No employer shall employ any of his or her employees for a work week longer than forty (40) hours, unless such employee receives compensation ... not less than one and one-half (1-1/2) times

sickLeave.note: No Kentucky law requires private employers to provide paid sick leave.

finalPay.fired: by the next normal pay period or within 14 days of separation, whichever is later
finalPay.quit: by the next normal pay period or within 14 days of separation, whichever is later
finalPay.ptoNote: Kentucky counts 'vested vacation pay' as wages, so vacation that is vested under the employer's policy or agreement must be paid with final wages.

source.quote: not later than the next normal pay period following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving or fourteen (14) days following such date ... whichever last occurs.

ptoSource.quote: "Wages" includes any compensation due to an employee by reason of his or her employment, including salaries, commissions, vested vacation pay

breaks.meal: A reasonable lunch period, as close to mid-shift as possible, starting no sooner than 3 hours and no later than 5 hours after the shift begins
breaks.rest: Paid rest period of at least 10 minutes for each 4 hours worked, in addition to the lunch period

source.quote: No employer shall require any employee to work without a rest period of at least ten (10) minutes during each four (4) hours worked ... No reduction in compensation shall be made

rightToWorkSource.quote: no employee shall be required, as a condition of employment or continuation of employment, to: 1. Become or remain a member of a labor organization; 2. Pay any dues

notes.text: Kentucky is one of the few states requiring paid 10-minute rest breaks for every 4 hours worked, plus a lunch period between the 3rd and 5th hour of the shift.

source.quote: In no case shall an employee be required to take a lunch period sooner than three (3) hours after his work shift commences, nor more than five (5) hours

notes.text: Seventh-day overtime: an employee permitted to work all seven days of a workweek (and more than 40 hours) earns time and a half for the seventh day.

source.quote: Any employer who permits any employee to work seven (7) days in any one (1) workweek shall pay him at the rate of time and a half for the time worked on the seventh day.

notes.text: Kentucky became a right-to-work state in January 2017.

source.quote: Amended 2017 Ky. Acts ch. 1, sec. 1, effective January 9, 2017.

uncertain: Education and Labor Cabinet website (elc.ky.gov, formerly labor.ky.gov) returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch; all values come from the KRS on apps.legislature.ky.gov (database updated 10/10/2026).
Paid sick leave: no state law to my knowledge, but no official page saying so was read; source null.
Local minimum wages: Louisville and Lexington ordinances were invalidated (2016 Kentucky Supreme Court); not re-verified on an official page today, localMinWages left empty.
Vacation payout coded 'policy': KRS 337.010 includes 'vested vacation pay' in wages, so whether vacation is owed depends on whether the employer's policy makes it vested.
Lunch period length is not set by statute ('reasonable period'); USDOL table describes it as 'ordinarily 1/2 hour', so mealMinutes left null.
